newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka Bank to use blocked forex as collateral.
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka Bank to use blocked forex as collateral.

text.p: Croatian commercial bank Zagrebacka Banka d.d. said on Friday it would allow citizens to get long-term loans collateralised by their blocked foreign exchange deposits.
Interest rates and other terms would remain unchanged, the bank said in a press release.
Until now Zagrebacka has granted loans to citizens using domestic or hard currency savings, deposited in the bank, as collateral.
Some 4.3 billion German marks in old foreign exchange deposits in Croatian banks was blocked by the National Bank of Yugoslavia before its 1991 breakup.

Since independence these liabilities have been turned into public debt but its servicing has been left to banks. The banks have also received bonds in lieu of payment for the first two instalments of the principal they owed to depositors.

To reduce the amount of debt, Croatian government has allowed the frozen hard currency to be used for purchases of state-owned flats and stocks. The outstanding debt is estimated at some 2.5 billion marks. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
